belief: I don't belong among successful people.
origins: Walking into a conference room, a neighborhood, a church gathering, or a social event where everyone seems more polished can bring a sudden sense of being an imposter. People who moved up from humble beginnings often describe it. We can feel that someone will soon “find out,” and so we stay quiet or stay away.
teaches: Paul writes that we are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household. We are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus. Paul also says, “Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.” God settles the lonely in families. Belonging in the family of God does not depend on being impressive, and the same welcome applies in every room we are called into.
self_statements: I am an imposter and they will find out.
I do not belong in this room.
They are on a different level than I am.
I should stay where I am comfortable.
errors: Believing that I am fooling people about my ability.
Assuming others see me as out of place.
Feeling out of place and concluding that I am.
questions: What qualified me to be in this room?
When have I felt like an outsider and later found I belonged?
What do I assume others think about me?
What does God say about my belonging?
What would I say to a friend who felt this way?
What is one small way I could take my place?
truth: I belong because God has welcomed me, and my invitation to a place is not a mistake. Success is not the ticket to belonging. I can walk into rooms with humility and quiet confidence and trust that I have something to offer.
hw_truths: Others feel out of place, too.
I can walk in with humble confidence.
log: Each week, note one time you stayed in a room where you felt out of place and what happened.
actions: Write the work, training, or character that earned your place.
Before a gathering, plan one question or comment to offer.
Look for one person who is friendly or who feels like an outsider too.
Pray Ephesians 2:19 before a hard room.
prayer: Lord, You have made me a member of Your household. Quiet the voice that says I do not belong. Help me walk into every room with humility and quiet confidence. Amen.
hw_questions: What qualifies me to be here?
When have I felt out of place and later belonged?
What do I fear others think?
What does God say about my belonging?
Who might be a friend in the room?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am a member of God’s household, so I belong wherever He sends me.”
